text:
ash: Quick sync: we're debating internal API shape for admin/control plane. Options: keep REST (path-based ops), move to gRPC+proto (typed), or accept both with gateway normalization. Need to think telemetry, quotas, SDK ergonomics, and rollout UX.
mika: Strong +1 for typed proto for internal services. Less brittle than path normalization. But I get ops concerns about exposing gRPC everywhere.
trent: From gateway perspective dual-protocol is doable but we must tie everything to a canonical operation id for metrics & quotas. If REST -> op-id header and gRPC -> op-id derived from :method, console can use op-id exclusively.
donna: UX question: how do we surface missing mappings? People will push new REST paths and forget to add op-id. We should show a per-route "mapping health" with counts of unmapped requests.
ash: Implementation sketch: Envoy rules add x-op-id for known REST routes; use envoy.filters.http.router header add for matched paths. For gRPC we add a Lua filter that maps :method -> x-op-id via a static table (loaded from config). That keeps tracing/metrics unified.
mika: Example Lua snippet idea:

```lua
local mapping = { ["/admin.Admin/GetUser"] = "admin.get_user" }
local method = ngx.req.get_headers()[":method"]
if mapping[method] then
  ngx.req.set_header("x-op-id", mapping[method])
end
```

trent: That works but Lua per-request adds CPU. For admin plane QPS it's fine. Don't do this on inference edge.
donna: Quotas: gateway-level quotas keyed by op-id + tenant. But we should also emit the op-id into the service request so services can do secondary quota checks (tenant isolation). So gateway short-circuits obvious bursts, services are authoritative.
ash: Telemetry: unify labels: operation.name=op-id, resource.service, tenant.id. Ensure distributed trace id propagation (x-request-id, traceparent). Console should have a route page with: mapping state (green/yellow/red), last 7d unmapped rate, representative trace sample button.
mika: SDK story: generate client libraries from proto for internal teams, but also ship small REST helpers that set x-op-id automatically. If a team uses REST but has no op-id we'll auto-insert a best-effort inferred op-id (path normalization) but mark it as inferred so console warns.
donna: Rollout UX: feature flag on route: "accept-grpc" and "require-op-id". During canary, set accept-grpc=true but require-op-id=false so we don't break teams. After mapping cleanup, flip require-op-id=true. Add a console bulk-mapper to tag multiple paths to op-ids.
trent: Observability impact: make sure metric names are stable (admin_gateway_request_total{operation="admin.get_user"}). Avoid embedding tenant in metric name; use labels.
ash: Ops-bot: deployed canary admin-gateway with mapping feature to staging. telemetry job: admin.gateway.prometheus. Looks healthy.
mika: One last: protobuf evolution. We should require forward/backward compatible changes for internal proto packages and keep a changelog. Also generate human readable operation ids from proto service+method.
nash: Agreed. Next steps action items: (1) add x-op-id header templates to gateway (trent), (2) implement Lua mapping for gRPC fallback (nash), (3) console: mapping health UI + flags (donna), (4) SDK helpers and proto generation docs (mika).
donna: I'll add the console ticket and a mockup. Leaving this thread open for follow-ups. Ping if you hit blockers. :wave:
